proofDescriptions.lean: Lean checks a formal statement from its assumptions.
proofDescriptions.written: A written argument for the stated result and assumptions.
proofDescriptions.explored: An open question with partial results or checked examples.

convolution-stability.scope: Written stability bounds for regular probability measures on locally compact Hausdorff groups and for positive states on finite Kac quantum groups, in the stated small-defect ranges.
convolution-stability.brief: A sharp leading bound on distance to a subgroup law, and a dimension-independent linear bound for finite quantum groups.

multiplication-tables.scope: The sharp lower bound concerns selected alphabets; the upper bound also applies to the complete multiplication table. The proof uses established circuit-to-stabilization and Hilbert-series results.
multiplication-tables.brief: A sharp worst-case stabilization bound over bounded integer sets, including an improved upper bound for the complete multiplication table.

geometry-recovery.scope: Written coefficient stability, convex moment reconstruction and sample-recovery bounds for fixed complexity and separated, bounded boundaries.
geometry-recovery.brief: Dimension-independent coefficient stability, convex reconstruction from label moments, and recovery bounds for corrupted samples.

binomial-residues.scope: For each fixed prime, a density-one set of columns attains every remainder modulo every power of the prime. A quantitative bound covers several primes simultaneously.
binomial-residues.brief: Almost every column of Pascal’s triangle attains every remainder modulo every power of a fixed prime, with a simultaneous bound for a growing range of primes.

hidden-stages.scope: Written threshold for populations with at most m exponential stages: the joint distribution of m matched totals identifies the population distribution of stage count and unordered rates, while m−1 can fail. Uniform estimator guarantees assume a positive rate floor.
hidden-stages.brief: An exact matched-repeat threshold for hidden exponential stages, with direct recovery of intervention responses.

factor-packing.scope: Written arithmetic repair and depth arguments. A correction of an earlier multiplication-table example gives larger families of missing elements and associated Picard-group consequences.
factor-packing.brief: Persistent factorization obstructions, larger families of missing elements, and a positive-proportion depth deficit.

distinct-products.scope: Written combinatorial and sieve arguments for the distinct-product bound.
distinct-products.brief: An upper bound toward the triple-product case of Erdős problem 425.

finite-symmetry.scope: Written proof of the 4/9 structure theorem and its exact extremal consequences in the specified finite abelian groups. Specific finite density, quotient and fibre deductions are also checked in Lean.
finite-symmetry.brief: Index-seven structure and exact extremal Cayley graphs in specified finite abelian groups.

recurring-prime-gaps.scope: Written four-point selection law and gcd classification using Merikoski’s corrected four-group sieve and a fixed CRT construction. The modular corollary also uses the finite-group structure theorem.
recurring-prime-gaps.brief: A four-point selection law restricts the greatest common divisor of recurring consecutive-prime gaps to 2, 4 or 6.

arithmetic-tensors.scope: Written finite tensor results and arithmetic transfer using external Koymans–Smith estimates. The later elliptic-curve deduction is conditional on the named Cassels-pairing and analytic inputs.
arithmetic-tensors.brief: Distribution and rank guarantees for prime-symbol arrays, with a further application to quadratic twists of an elliptic curve.

matching-stability.scope: Written global matching theorem. Constants depend on the number of boundaries and the threshold bound, independently of ambient dimension; colliding boundaries are allowed.
matching-stability.brief: A linear bound matches Gaussian decision boundaries even when coincident boundaries cancel.

prime-patterns.scope: Lean checks the matching-based gap deduction assuming the quantitative Selberg estimate and the labelled Bennett–Frieze matching theorem. The stronger Rankin-style gap bound has a written proof.
prime-patterns.brief: Two constructions bound the length of gaps among prime-pattern candidates. Lean checks the matching-based deduction under two stated hypotheses.
